Upward walk mechanics and the inactive and active transition handlers, including child mask handling and expiry propagation order.

findings.text: Per CPU timer migration deactivation for idle entry accepts a next expiry hint and reports the earliest relevant group expiry. When migration support is unavailable the hint passes through unchanged. Otherwise the calling CPU context is marked idle and its wakeup marker is published so a concurrent idle path reevaluation cannot overlook an event.

Per CPU timer migration activation ends the idle state. It clears the idle marker, marks the local CPU event as ignored for upward propagation, resets the wakeup marker to the indefinite value, and propagates the change toward the hierarchy root. A header fallback provides an empty variant for configurations without migration support.

Active path fast query estimates the next global event without deactivating. It passes the caller hint through when migration is unavailable, reports indefinite when the local group is not both migrator owned and lonely or when any ancestor is not lonely, and otherwise folds the caller hint with each ancestor cached next expiry up to the root.

The maximum time value denotes absence of an expiry across migration and tick handling. It means no global timer is armed, the local timer wins, the CPU is going offline, or the tick should remain stopped, and it disables propagation or programming in those cases.

Group ownership and solitude are derived from an atomic state snapshot. Migrator ownership holds when the recorded migrator equals the caller child mask or equals the none value. Solitude holds when the active set contains at most one member. The combined predicate requires both.

Activation and deactivation serialize against concurrent migration state changes with the per CPU migration lock, covering the idle flag, wakeup publication and upward walk. The fast query and the idle clearing path are intentionally lock free on the fast path, relying on atomic group state and ordered single word accesses, accepting a rare redundant remote wakeup rather than taking a lock on idle exit.

Timer base idle management offers a try to idle query and an unconditional clear. The query reports indefinite immediately if already idle and otherwise asks for the next interrupt and its idle outcome. The clear resets the local base idle marker, and on full dynticks CPUs also the global marker, then triggers migration activation without holding the base lock.

On builds without symmetric multiprocessing timer migration support the timer selection helper only ensures the local event choice carries the minimum of the local and global candidates so an early global timer is not overlooked.

Each CPU migration context cycles between active and idle. Deactivation with a concrete expiry clears the ignore marker on the CPU event so it participates upward, while deactivation with the indefinite value leaves it ignored. Activation always sets ignore and announces indefinite wakeup before walking upward.

Tick scheduler operation is governed by persistent flags. In idle entry the in idle and idle active markers are set with an entry timestamp; exit clears them and wakes the scheduler clock. Stopping sets the stopped marker after recording load and quiet state plus the last tick deadline, while restart and full tick updates clear it and rearm the tick. The do timer last marker remembers jiffies duty handover.

Tick stopping first marks the timer base idle and clamps any later expiry to the earlier computed deadline to avoid oversleep on shallow idle states. If the base is busy the tick is retained. Otherwise jiffies duty is handed off if held, unchanged deadlines short circuit reprogramming, indefinite deadlines cancel or park the event, and concrete deadlines arm either a pinned absolute high resolution timer or a low resolution event with a matching software deadline.

Idle tick stopping is refused when the scheduler tick lacks nohz enablement, when rescheduling is pending, when pending soft interrupt work survives hotplug and realtime blocking filters, and on full dynticks systems when the caller holds timekeeping duty or when no timekeeper is designated, the latter being treated as unexpected.

Idle and interrupt boundaries form the outward tick interface. Idle entry asserts enabled interrupts before taking the local CPU state and sleeping the scheduler clock. Idle exit and restart paths run with interrupts disabled, stop dynticks accounting and restart a stopped tick. Interrupt entry wakes the clock and refreshes jiffies when stopped, while interrupt exit either sleeps the clock and refreshes entry time in idle or refreshes the full tick outside idle. An empty interrupt entry variant exists for configurations without this handling.

Sleep length estimation exposes the interval until the next timed event for idle governors. It starts from the device deadline relative to idle entry, refuses to advance when stopping is disallowed, otherwise queries the next tick event and folds in the earliest high resolution deadline excluding the scheduler timer itself. Companion queries expose the raw device deadline and the per CPU idle attempt counter.

Per CPU tick scheduler state contains flags, stalled_jiffies and last_tick_jiffies for stall tracking, sched_timer with last_tick next_tick idle_waketime and got_idle_tick for handling, idle_entrytime for entry timing, last_jiffies timer_expires_base timer_expires next_timer idle_expires idle_calls and idle_sleeps for stop accounting, tick_dep_mask for full dynticks dependencies, and check_clocks for clocksource changes.
Tick device state holds evtdev pointer and mode selector. Mode uses an enumeration with TICKDEV_MODE_PERIODIC and TICKDEV_MODE_ONESHOT as its two distinct values.

Tick scheduler flag positions are fixed: in idle occupies bit zero, stopped occupies bit one, idle active occupies bit two, do timer last occupies bit three, nohz enablement occupies bit four, high resolution mode occupies bit five.
The tick scheduler header guard is defined to prevent reinclusion, and the old time type syscall selector is defined as enabled for the time implementation.

Second granularity time syscalls provide read and set operations. The read variants return real seconds since the epoch and optionally store the value to user memory while forcing a successful return encoding. The set variants read seconds from user memory, attach zero subsecond time, enforce time setting permission, then apply the new wall time.

Microsecond wall time and timezone syscalls share validation and copy semantics. Reads fill seconds and truncated microseconds from real time and optionally copy out the global timezone. Writes validate microsecond range and configuration gates for old or compat time types, convert microseconds to nanoseconds, optionally fetch a timezone from user memory, then delegate to the common 64 bit setter.

Clock tuning syscalls copy a control structure between user and kernel, delegate adjustment to a common routine, and copy the result back. The 32 bit time variant translates through an intermediate native representation on both entry and exit. Faults during copy or translation fail the call.

Several misuses are treated as programming errors with one time warnings. Fast expiry query while idle, activation while not idle, idle entry with a pending expiry base, exit without in idle state or with a pending base, stopping an offline CPU, and missing timekeeper on full dynticks each warn without crashing.

Lost wakeup and oversleep hazards shape the design. Deactivation publishes the computed wakeup with ordering so idle reevaluation cannot miss an event. Stopping clamps a recomputed later deadline back to the earlier value used for idle state selection and sanity checks programmed clock state before skipping reprogramming. Idle entry accounting avoids double counting tiny intervals on repeated stop within one idle trip.

Full dynticks maintenance runs only on full dynticks CPUs with nohz active. When stopping is allowed it stops through the idle stop path, otherwise it restarts a previously stopped tick. The idle update variant delegates to this logic on full dynticks CPUs and to unconditional restart elsewhere. Retain paths only clear the expiry base marker.

Low resolution tick handling parks the device deadline to indefinite and clears the forced marker before invoking the common tick handler. A restart request from that handler reprograms the device for the scheduler timer deadline.
The got idle tick marker is a consuming boolean. Reading it when set clears it and reports presence, otherwise reports absence.

Top level interrupt entry first performs a one shot broadcast check for this CPU then runs the nohz interrupt entry. A boot parameter stores an integer skew value for scheduler tick spreading at init time.

Pending soft interrupt work during idle tick stop consideration emits a rate limited warning identifying the pending set, bounded to a small number of reports, and vetoes stopping unless the work is hotplug safe on an inactive CPU or realtime handling is blocked.

Idle stop attempts increment an attempt counter on every evaluation, while successful stops with a positive deadline additionally increment a sleep counter and record the sleep deadline. Restart and exit paths stop dynticks accounting exactly when leaving a stopped state.
A single global timezone object holds the system timezone shared by the get and compat get paths for copy out and updated through the common set path.
